meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 8 — Chip manufacturing depth + international deals that protect or preserve Taiwan’s economic security and de-facto sovereignty space. Focuses on US–Taiwan economic-security architecture (Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, 21st-Century Trade Initiative, investment/reshoring MOUs), semiconductor supply-chain resilience, and the AI-demand context. Explicit referenced_by lists for force-layout edge strength.
meta.strategy_note: User request: explore chip manufacturing further and the international deals protecting/preserving Taiwan’s sovereignty amid China–USA tension and AI chip demand. These instruments are economic-statecraft nodes that sit at the intersection of trade, technology and security; they create high-authority edges into the semiconductor cluster already built.

candidates.title: US–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (ART) — AIT–TECRO
candidates.publisher: American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) / Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (TECRO)
candidates.description: Major economic agreement signed February 2026 under AIT–TECRO auspices. Eliminates or reduces tariffs on up to 99 % of Taiwan’s tariff lines for US goods, addresses non-tariff barriers, includes investment-facilitation and supply-chain resilience provisions, and contains explicit economic-security alignment language (including triggers related to ‘covered nations’). Pending full domestic formalities but already the most significant bilateral trade instrument in decades.
referenced_by: Taiwan trade statistics and FTA-network analysis
Semiconductor and critical-supply-chain policy documents
US and Taiwan official fact sheets and subsequent implementation reporting
candidates.notes: Highest-value recent economic-security node. Functions as both a market-access instrument and a geopolitical alignment device. Creates strong edges into the semiconductor cluster (preferential treatment, investment facilitation, export-control coordination) and into the broader US–Taiwan relationship architecture.

candidates.title: United States–Taiwan Initiative on 21st-Century Trade (first agreement)
candidates.description: First agreement under the Initiative (signed 2023, entered into force December 2024) covering anti-corruption, good regulatory practices, customs and trade facilitation, services domestic regulation, and SMEs. Foundation layer on which the later Agreement on Reciprocal Trade builds.
referenced_by: US–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade
Customs and trade-facilitation statistics and reform documents
TIFA Council and subsequent negotiation records
candidates.notes: Foundational US–Taiwan trade instrument of the 2020s. Provides the regulatory and facilitation base that the deeper ART then expands into market access and economic-security commitments.

candidates.title: AIT–TECRO Memorandum of Understanding on industrial parks, semiconductor investment and supply-chain cooperation (Jan 2026)
candidates.description: MOU under which Taiwan commits to facilitate large-scale investment by Taiwanese firms into US semiconductor, AI, energy and related industrial parks/clusters, with financial support from the Taiwan side; US side provides preferential treatment considerations in Section 232 and related investigations. Explicitly links semiconductor capacity expansion in the United States to the bilateral economic-security partnership.
referenced_by: US–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade fact sheets
Semiconductor investment and reshoring announcements
Science-park and advanced-capacity statistics (outbound investment side)
candidates.notes: Direct bridge between the semiconductor manufacturing cluster and the sovereignty-protecting economic architecture. Large announced investment figures (hundreds of billions) make this a high-mass edge into both the chip and the US–Taiwan nodes.

candidates.title: US–Taiwan Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (TIFA) Council
candidates.description: Long-standing consultative framework under which the two sides address trade and investment issues. Continues to serve as the institutional venue for monitoring and expanding the economic relationship.
referenced_by: 21st-Century Trade Initiative and ART negotiation records
Bilateral trade-policy documents
candidates.notes: Institutional continuity node for the unofficial relationship.

candidates.title: Taiwan Relations Act (US) — economic and security context for AIT–TECRO framework
candidates.jurisdiction_level: international (US domestic law with Taiwan effects)
candidates.description: US domestic statute (1979) that provides the legal basis for the unofficial relationship conducted through AIT and for continued commercial, cultural and security-related interaction. All subsequent AIT–TECRO trade and investment instruments rest on this foundation.
referenced_by: All AIT–TECRO agreements and fact sheets
US Taiwan policy and economic-security documents
candidates.notes: Foundational recurring-citation node for the entire unofficial economic architecture. Without it the later trade and investment instruments would lack their institutional channel.

candidates.title: Taiwanese semiconductor investment and capacity expansion in the United States (official and reported figures)
candidates.publisher: MOEA / Investment Commission / US Commerce / industry reporting cited in official releases
candidates.description: Statistics and official commitments concerning Taiwanese semiconductor firms’ direct investment and capacity build-out in the United States (fabs, packaging, materials, equipment ecosystem). Figures in the hundreds of billions have been associated with the recent AIT–TECRO investment understandings.
referenced_by: AIT–TECRO investment MOU and ART fact sheets
Science-park and advanced-process capacity indicators (outbound side)
BOP financial-account and outbound-investment statistics
candidates.notes: Quantifies the physical manifestation of the economic-security partnership. Creates concrete edges from the domestic semiconductor cluster into the US–Taiwan architecture and into global supply-chain resilience analysis.

candidates.title: AI-related demand impact on Taiwan semiconductor production and export statistics
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs / DGBAS / industry sources cited officially
candidates.description: Statistical and official commentary linking the surge in AI server, high-performance computing and advanced-packaging demand to the record growth rates in electronic-components and computers/optical production indices, science-park IC revenue, and related export orders.
referenced_by: Electronic Components and Computers/Optical production series
Science-park IC revenue
Export orders and semiconductor trade statistics
candidates.notes: Demand-side narrative node that explains the extreme recent growth rates. Essential for understanding why the semiconductor cluster currently carries such high centrality and authority in the graph.

candidates.title: Export-control and technology-security alignment with the United States
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economic Affairs / related agencies / AIT–TECRO instruments
candidates.description: Policy and statistical traces of Taiwan’s alignment with US-led export-control regimes on advanced semiconductors and related technologies. Appears in ART security architecture language and in domestic implementation measures.
referenced_by: US–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (security provisions)
Semiconductor trade and advanced-process statistics
Industrial and national-security policy documents
candidates.notes: Security-layer node that links the commercial semiconductor cluster to the sovereignty-protecting economic architecture.

candidates.title: New Southbound Policy — technology and semiconductor diplomacy components
candidates.description: Policy framework that leverages Taiwan’s semiconductor, AI and trusted-industry strengths to deepen economic and technology ties with Southeast Asian and South Asian partners, thereby diversifying international space.
referenced_by: Outbound investment and trade statistics with Southbound partners
Semiconductor and digital-industry policy documents
Regional economic-cooperation agreements
candidates.notes: Diversification node that complements the US-centric economic-security architecture. Uses the same semiconductor/AI assets to expand Taiwan’s international economic space.

candidates.title: Taiwan semiconductor–economic-security–sovereignty architecture (meta-node)
candidates.publisher: Derived from AIT–TECRO instruments, MOEA, NSTC and CBC sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that binds the domestic semiconductor manufacturing cluster (production, science parks, advanced capacity, trade) to the international instruments that protect and expand Taiwan’s economic security and de-facto international space (ART, 21st-Century Trade Initiative, investment MOUs, TIFA, export-control alignment, New Southbound technology diplomacy).
referenced_by: All detailed semiconductor and US–Taiwan economic-security nodes in Batches 7 and 8
Cross-strait statistics and ECFA (as the contrasting relationship)
National accounts, BOP and R&D series that treat electronics as the strategic sector
candidates.notes: Highest-level integrating node for the user’s requested theme. Allows the force layout to treat ‘chips + the deals that protect the chip island’ as a single high-mass, geopolitically charged object rather than disconnected commercial and diplomatic leaves.
